verificationRecords.scope: slice s21 real Graph3D lease caller

progress.summary: Slice s21 hardens the existing two-context WebGL pool with cancellable capacity-reserving scheduled waiters. A moving twelve-passage window stays at active<=2 and waiting<=1, preserves the focused lease, cleans to 0/0, and the real Graph3D host still releases on switch/context loss.

expectedLearning: Whether route-local capabilities and build-time math materially reduce publication closure while preserved visual truth, whether pages scale by active passages rather than total passages, and whether economics plus physics prove a minimal renderer-neutral graph lifecycle.
allowedWork: Economics route capability closure, deterministic build-time lesson and KaTeX artifacts, retained dynamic math, economics CSS ownership and verified pruning.
Multi-passage lifecycle, production pressure fixtures, one page scroll coordinator, bounded near-viewport hydration, stable placeholders, offscreen pause, capability reuse, and WebGL lease pressure.

Physics-local retained SVG runtime, two-caller Graph2D lifecycle extraction, renderer-neutral Graph3D protocol, existing internal Graph3D host adoption, focused tests, performance evidence, project memory, and Theseus control records.
disallowedWork: Do not resume matrix or Lisp animation work, add another tutorial or curriculum domain, build SvelteKit, Internal Studio, Public Web, or either editor.
Do not delete rollback lesson layouts, introduce a universal scene graph, migrate every graph caller, or make Three.js, KaTeX, code, or WebGL an eager shared dependency.
Do not redesign the approved economics or physics visual language, change semantic truth, accessibility, direct seek, rewind, URL meaning, Review identity, or current performance ceilings.
